cqa_tuples.knowledge_point: Define the purpose of IPv6 extension headers
cqa_tuples.target_criteria: FULL = at least 2 parts (extend fixed header / optional network-layer info); PARTIAL = exactly 1; ABSENT = 0
acceptable_variants: headers that add extra features to the base IPv6 header
optional fields for extra network layer data
used to add more information beyond the standard header
extra headers for optional network layer functions
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: Extension headers are used to extend the fixed IPv6 header with additional, optional network layer information.

cqa_tuples.knowledge_point: Identify the location of extension headers in an IPv6 packet
cqa_tuples.target_criteria: any of: between fixed header and payload / between main header and upper-layer or transport header
evidence_facets: between main header and transport-layer header
acceptable_variants: placed after the main header but before the data
located between the base header and the transport layer
inserted after the fixed header and before the upper-layer header
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: If present, they are located between the fixed header/main header and payload/upper-layer header/transport-layer header.

cqa_tuples.knowledge_point: Explain the main advantage of extension headers over IPv4
cqa_tuples.target_criteria: any of: appending new options without changing header / faster processing by intermediate devices (ONE advantage is FULL)
evidence_facets: appending new options without changing the header
acceptable_variants: allows adding new options without modifying the base header
intermediate routers process packets faster because they ignore most options
more efficient processing compared to IPv4
easier to add new features without header changes
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: It allows the appending of new options without changing the header. IPv6 packets with optional headers are typically processed faster/simpler by intermediate devices.
